strings.name: Iga Świątek
strings.summary: Świątek became Poland’s first major singles champion at nineteen by winning Roland-Garros in 2020. Heavy topspin, movement and aggressive baseline play brought her the No.1 ranking, four French Opens, a US Open and Wimbledon. In 2024 she accepted a one-month suspension after a positive test traced to contaminated medication. A thigh injury ended her 2026 season early.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. Selected career milestones; results and records refer to their cited dates, not an exhaustive results log or live ranking.
strings.influence.rationale: A major champion and world No.1 who strengthened Poland's competitive influence in world tennis.
strings.facts.fact-1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-2.label: Sporting family
strings.facts.fact-2.value: Her father Tomasz competed in rowing at the 1988 Olympics
strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Poland’s major breakthrough
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Won the 2020 French Open without losing a set, becoming Poland’s first major singles champion.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Major titles on three surfaces
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: A 6–0, 6–0 Wimbledon final win in 2025 added a grass major to her clay and hard-court titles.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Season ended by thigh injury
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Withdrew from Ningbo and ended her season because of a left-thigh injury, ending her WTA Finals qualifying bid.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: First Wimbledon title
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Beat Amanda Anisimova 6–0, 6–0 for her sixth major singles title and first at Wimbledon.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Accepted a one-month suspension
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Accepted a one-month ban after a trimetazidine positive test was traced to contaminated melatonin medication; the violation was found unintentional.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Fourth French Open title
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Defeated Jasmine Paolini for a third consecutive French Open and fourth overall.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: WTA Finals champion
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Won the Cancun WTA Finals unbeaten, defeating Jessica Pegula in the final and finishing the year at No.1.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: US Open champion
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Defeated Ons Jabeur to win her first hard-court major at the US Open.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: First world No.1 ranking
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Became Poland’s first singles No.1 during a season featuring 37 consecutive wins and six straight titles.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: First French Open title
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Won her first tour-level title at Roland-Garros without losing a set, aged nineteen.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: Junior Wimbledon champion
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Won the Wimbledon girls’ singles title before moving toward the senior tour.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Warsaw
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in Warsaw and took up tennis after her older sister; her father had competed in Olympic rowing.
